title: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Circuit Malfunction
problem: The Engine Control Unit (ECU) detects an implausible signal from the MAP sensor, indicating a general circuit issue.
symptoms: Engine hesitation; Poor acceleration; Increased fuel consumption
actions: Check sensor wiring for damage or corrosion; Test MAP sensor output voltage; Replace MAP sensor if faulty
location: Usually mounted on or near the intake manifold.

title: MAP Sensor Circuit Low Input
problem: The ECU receives a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is lower than the expected operating range, often indicating a short to ground or faulty sensor.
symptoms: Rough idle; Stalling; Lack of power
actions: Inspect MAP sensor wiring for shorts; Verify vacuum line integrity; Replace MAP sensor
location: Usually mounted on or near the intake manifold.

title: MAP Sensor Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU receives a voltage signal from the MAP sensor that is higher than the expected operating range, often indicating an open circuit or faulty sensor.
symptoms: Poor acceleration; High fuel consumption; Engine runs rich
actions: Check MAP sensor wiring for opens; Test MAP sensor resistance; Replace MAP sensor
location: Usually mounted on or near the intake manifold.

symptoms: Engine warning light on; Engine power reduction; Engine may shut down

title: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary circuit that controls the fuel pump, preventing proper fuel delivery.
symptoms: Engine no start; Engine stalls while riding; Loss of power

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the CKP sensor, indicating a general circuit issue or inability to read engine RPM.

title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Range/Performance
problem: The ECU detects an implausible signal from the CKP sensor, indicating that the signal is outside expected range or performance.
symptoms: Intermittent engine cutout; Erratic RPM readings; Hard starting

title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the CMP sensor, indicating a general circuit issue or inability to read cam position for ignition timing.
symptoms: Engine hard starting; Poor engine performance; Loss of power
actions: Inspect CMP sensor wiring for damage; Test CMP sensor resistance; Replace CMP sensor

title: Ignition Coil 'A' Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the primary or secondary circuit of the ignition coil for cylinder 1, leading to no spark.
symptoms: Engine misfire; Rough idle; Loss of power
actions: Check ignition coil wiring; Test ignition coil resistance; Replace ignition coil

title: EVAP Purge Control Valve Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the circuit controlling the EVAP purge valve, affecting fuel vapor recovery.
symptoms: Engine rough idle; Increased emissions; Fuel smell
actions: Inspect purge valve wiring; Test purge valve operation; Replace purge valve
location: Connected to the EVAP canister and intake manifold.

title: Fuel Level Sensor Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the fuel level sensor, indicating a general circuit issue or incorrect fuel level reading.
symptoms: Inaccurate fuel gauge; Fuel light malfunction; Unknown fuel range
actions: Check fuel level sensor wiring; Test fuel level sensor resistance; Replace fuel level sensor

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the VSS, indicating a general circuit issue or incorrect vehicle speed reading.
symptoms: Inaccurate speedometer; Cruise control malfunction; Erratic shifting (if applicable)
actions: Inspect VSS wiring for damage; Clean VSS; Replace VSS
location: Mounted on the transmission or wheel hub.

title: Idle Air Control System Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects a fault in the IAC system, leading to improper regulation of engine idle speed.
symptoms: High or low idle; Engine stalls at idle; Erratic idle
actions: Clean IAC valve; Check IAC valve wiring; Replace IAC valve

title: System Voltage Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal system voltage, indicating issues with the battery or charging system.
symptoms: Dim lights; Hard starting; Engine stalling
actions: Check battery terminals; Test battery voltage; Inspect rectifier/regulator

title: System Voltage Low
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently below the specified minimum threshold.
symptoms: Hard starting; Dim headlights; Electronic components malfunction
actions: Charge battery; Test charging system (stator/rectifier); Inspect battery terminals

title: System Voltage High
problem: The ECU detects that the system voltage is consistently above the specified maximum threshold.
symptoms: Bulb burnout; Battery overcharging; Electronic component damage
actions: Test rectifier/regulator output; Inspect battery condition; Check charging circuit wiring

title: Serial Communication Link Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects a malfunction in the serial communication link, preventing proper data exchange with other modules.
symptoms: No communication with diagnostic tool; Multiple system warnings; Engine performance issues
actions: Check wiring harness for damage; Inspect connector pins; Consult wiring diagram for communication lines

title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
problem: The ECU detects an internal error within its Read Only Memory (ROM), indicating a critical internal hardware fault.
symptoms: Engine no start; Engine stalls; Unpredictable engine behavior
actions: Attempt ECU firmware update (if possible); Replace ECU

title: ECU/PCM Processor Fault
problem: The ECU detects a fault within its main processor, indicating a critical internal hardware malfunction.
symptoms: Engine no start; Multiple system failures; Random shutdowns
actions: Replace ECU

title: Immobilizer Communication Error
problem: The ECU fails to communicate with the immobilizer unit, preventing engine start or operation.
symptoms: Engine cranks but no start; Security light flashing; Key not recognized
actions: Check immobilizer antenna; Inspect wiring between ECU and immobilizer; Re-register key

title: Lean Angle Sensor Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an abnormal signal from the lean angle sensor, which is designed to cut off fuel/ignition in case of a tip-over.

title: Side Stand Switch Circuit Open

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open

actions: Inspect TAC motor wiring; Check throttle body for obstructions; Replace throttle body

title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Range/Performance
problem: The ECU detects that the TAC motor is not operating within its expected range or performance parameters.

actions: Perform throttle body calibration; Check for mechanical binding; Replace throttle body

title: Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor 'D' Circuit Low Input

title: Accelerator Pedal Position Sensor 'D' Circuit High Input
problem: The ECU receives a voltage signal from the APP sensor (or ride-by-wire grip sensor) that is higher than expected.
symptoms: Unintended acceleration; Engine surging; Engine in limp mode
actions: Inspect APP sensor wiring for opens; Test APP sensor output; Replace APP sensor
location: Handlebar grip assembly (for ride-by-wire) or foot pedal assembly.

title: Fan Motor Circuit Open/Short
problem: The ECU detects an open or short circuit in the cooling fan motor, preventing proper engine cooling.
symptoms: Engine overheating; Fan not running when hot; Engine warning light
actions: Inspect fan motor wiring; Test fan motor for continuity; Replace fan motor

title: Headlight Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical anomaly in the headlight circuit.
symptoms: Headlights not working; Dim headlights; Flickering headlights
actions: Check headlight bulbs; Inspect headlight wiring harness; Test headlight switch

title: Tail Light Circuit Malfunction
problem: The ECU detects an electrical anomaly in the tail light circuit.
symptoms: Tail lights not working; Brake light issues; License plate light failure
actions: Check tail light bulbs; Inspect tail light wiring harness; Test tail light fuse

problem: The ABS module detects an implausible signal from the front wheel speed sensor, indicating a fault in the ABS system.

title: ABS Sensor Fault (Rear)
problem: The ABS module detects an implausible signal from the rear wheel speed sensor, indicating a fault in the ABS system.
symptoms: ABS warning light on; ABS system disabled; Loss of ABS function
actions: Inspect rear ABS sensor wiring; Clean rear ABS sensor; Replace rear ABS sensor
location: Mounted on the rear wheel hub or swingarm.

problem: The immobilizer unit detects an internal fault, preventing proper security function and engine start.
symptoms: Engine cranks but no start; Security light solid on; Key not recognized

title: Gear Position Sensor Malfunction
